chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Mu'min narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Isma'il al-Abdi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman (or al-Hasan), from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of 'Arafah, Allah will register for him one million Hajj with the Qa'im (peace be upon him) and one million 'Umrah with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and freeing one million slaves, and carrying one million horses in the way of Allah. And Allah will call him, 'My truthful slave who believed in My promise.' And the angels will say, 'So-and-so is truthful; Allah has purified him from above His Throne.' And he will be called 'Karub' on earth.

key_terms.قَبْرَ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him)
key_terms.كَرُوباً: Karub (a title meaning close or purified)
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: The Day of 'Arafah (9th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for visiting Imam Husayn's grave on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: Compiled by Ibn Qulawayh in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith underscores the unique merit of combining the pilgrimage to Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) with the Day of 'Arafah, a date deeply significant in Shia eschatology as the day of the Mahdi's emergence. The enumeration of rewards—such as a million Hajjs and the title 'Karub' (Close One)—reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt and the spiritual elevation attained through devotional visitation.
